subject: Final OKR adjudication + QBR comms playbook
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Draft rubric & proposed final procedure for Q2 OKR adjudication

Team —

Attached is a working rubric (QBR_score_rubric_v3.xlsx) that combines evidentiary thresholds with manager calibration notes. I want us to close the final adjudication this week so we can publish the narrative to the org and prep the customer-facing QBR pack for our top accounts (ACME included).

Please review the rubric and reply with:
- Anything that would materially change a score (e.g., missed evidence, metric rebaselining)
- Any objections to the proposed publish timeline below

Proposed timeline:
- Tue morning: managers submit final tags and evidence links
- Tue afternoon: senior calibration call (30m)
- Wed: I sign off and we generate the narrative + highlight reel
- Fri: comms go out to org and select customers

I want explicit note on any items we plan to escalate to execs for judgement. For ACME, Laura — we should reconcile the sample logs and the anomaly window before finalizing their "reliability" assessment.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: QBR_score_rubric_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft rubric & proposed final procedure for Q2 OKR adjudication

Vivek —

Quick read done. A few notes inline and one higher-level ask: can we treat any ACME-related reliability windows that lack audit log continuity as "insufficient evidence" unless product ops produce the missing KV cache traces?

Inline highlights:
- Rubric row 4 (quality regressions): tighten language to account for model variants in Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Evidence portal: add a required "sample prompt set + outputs" link for any customer-facing feature score > 3
- Publication schedule: suggest pushing customer-targeted comms to Thursday EOD to give our CS leads time to prep

I'll collate the manager tags today and upload a consolidated evidence bundle to the drive link.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft rubric & proposed final procedure for Q2 OKR adjudication

All —

Uploaded my team tags. Flag on ACME: we have two infra incidents in May that are borderline for the "uptime" threshold. I marked them as "needs adjudication" and attached the incident timeline in the evidence folder (customer_evidence_bundle_ACME.zip). If we require stricter audit logs I can pull the per-GPU telemetry but it will take until Wednesday morning.

Also: small ask on the calibration call — can we allocate 10 minutes to re-check the cross-functional dependency impact scoring? The current rubric weights that at 15% and my read is it should be 10%.

Jonas
Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: customer_evidence_bundle_ACME.zip (archive)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft rubric & proposed final procedure for Q2 OKR adjudication

Thanks, Vivek —

I reviewed the manager submissions and there are three cases where the evidence is sparse: ACME reliability (same as Jonas called out), MSC internal rollout (missing A/B logs), and the Experimentation OKR (we have results but the statistical test detail is incomplete). I think those should be flagged as "evidence insufficient" and we should default to conservative scoring for the QBR narrative.

I propose the following language for publication (short paragraph we can paste into the narrative):
"Where evidence is incomplete, Redwood defaulted to conservative scoring; teams have been asked to provide detailed logs and statistical tests for post-QBR review. Scores marked 'evidence insufficient' are provisional and subject to re-opened adjudication."

If that's acceptable, I'll draft the org-facing note and the customer-facing line for ACME.

Marissa
Head of GTM Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft rubric & proposed final procedure for Q2 OKR adjudication

Team —

I did a pass on the numbers and endorse the conservative approach for anything lacking primary telemetry. Two small operational asks for the calibration call:
1) Can someone from Reliability confirm the window boundaries so scoring can be consistent?
2) Laura — once you upload the sample prompt sets for any customer-facing features, can you also tag which model variant was used (hosted vs dedicated)?

I will join the calibration call and be prepared to sign off on the finance/comp implications for any score shifts that affect bonus payouts.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Finance & Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Emily Diaz <emily.d@acmecorp.com>
Cc: ACME - Product Steering <steering@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final scores published + QBR comms playbook (customer note for ACME)

Team & Emily —

Thank you for the quick turnaround. We completed the senior calibration this afternoon and I signed off on the final grades. Key decisions to record here: 

- Where evidence was incomplete (ACME uptime windows, internal A/B logs, experimentation stats), we applied the conservative policy and marked those scores provisional. Those items are flagged for re-opened adjudication once teams deliver missing telemetry.
- ACME reliability final: 3/5 (provisional) — see attached final_scores_published_20270702.pdf for the full breakdown.
- Communications plan: org-facing narrative will go out Monday 12:00PM PT; customer-targeted notes (ACME) will be sent Monday 3:00PM PT to allow CS time to prepare the call.

Emily — attached is the customer-facing paragraph we plan to include in the QBR pack. It is intentionally conservative and invites you to provide any additional logs you prefer we include for the final adjudication. If ACME wants us to re-open the reliability score before August review, please forward any supplementary telemetry to laura@redwood.com and jonas@redwood.com by July 16.

Draft customer paragraph (for your review):
"Redwood concluded that reliability performance during the quarter met expected standards overall. During two short windows we observed degraded throughput; our initial audit did not locate complete external audit logs for the full anomaly window. As a result, the reliability assessment for this quarter is provisional. We welcome additional telemetry to support a final review and adjustment prior to the next cycle."

Actions assigned: 
- Laura: publish org narrative and upload final evidence bundle to drive (due Mon 11:00AM PT).
- Marissa: finalize customer communications and coordinate CS dry-run (due Mon 2:00PM PT).
- Jonas: pull per-GPU telemetry if ACME supplies permit and upload by Jul 16.
- Karthik: confirm comp/finance downstream impacts for provisional scores and notify People Ops if any payouts are delayed.

Attachments: final_scores_published_20270702.pdf, QBR_score_rubric_v3.xlsx

I'll send the org comms template separately for review. Great work closing this quickly.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Product & Ops
Redwood Inference
